structure.heading: Enterprise Risk Register Scope, Method, and Rating Scale (FY2026)
text_content: **Enterprise Risk Register Scope, Method, and Rating Scale (FY2026)**

The register documents the enterprise-level exposure for 12 enterprise risks assessed as of 2026-04-30 and applies across all principal corporate functions, including Finance, Technology, Operations, Compliance, Human Resources, and Sales. Inclusion criteria focus on materiality to strategic objectives and enterprise continuity; project- and activity-level issues are assessed in subordinate registers. The scope encompasses strategic, operational, financial, compliance, reputational, and cyber domains, and is maintained by the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Office to support Board- and executive-level decision-making and resource prioritization and third party risks.

Methodology for assessment applies standardized scoring: Likelihood and Impact are each scored on a 1–5 scale to produce consistent inputs, and Residual Risk is calculated as Likelihood × Impact, yielding a numeric range of 1–25. For example, a probability score of 4 and impact score of 4 produces a Residual Risk of 16. The register records the assessed values and supports categorization; any Residual Risk ≥ 15 is classified as High. Calibration workshops with business-unit leads align scoring and document inter-rater adjustments per protocol.

Control effectiveness is rated on a 0–100% scale and is assessed through a combination of control testing, key risk indicators (KRIs), and evidence reviews conducted by Internal Audit and the ERM Office. For governance clarity the register uses tiered interpretation bands: controls rated below 50% are considered ineffective, 50–80% indicate partially effective controls requiring remediation, and above 80% are considered effective. Control test cycles run quarterly with exception reporting; corrective actions must include target remediation dates and owners to close gaps within 90 days.

Governance of the register is managed by the ERM Office and Chief Risk Officer, with reporting to the CEO, Executive Committee, and Audit Committee. Risk owners retain accountability for maintenance of risk entries, evidence, and remediation timelines; the ERM Office publishes a quarterly summary for executive review. Escalation protocols require the CRO to receive exception reports within 10 business days when control performance materially deteriorates or when risk exposure increases beyond agreed tolerances. The register and supporting documentation are retained five years and archived.

structure.heading: Top Residual Risks and Risk Owner Accountabilities (Q2 FY2026)
text_content: **Top Residual Risks and Risk Owner Accountabilities (Q2 FY2026)**

The register identifies R-03 Ransomware & destructive malware with Residual Risk 20 as the top residual risk; ownership is assigned to the CISO (Aisha Khan). This risk drives prioritized investment in endpoint protection, incident response, and backup integrity testing. Quarterly tabletop exercises and a 95% patch compliance target are mandated to reduce exploit windows and support measurable residual risk reduction. Status reporting occurs monthly.

30. High-risk items concentrate in cyber, supply chain, third-party concentration, and strategic execution; each has an assigned owner and documented treatment plan. Risk owners report monthly status, percentage mitigation achieved, and upcoming milestones. Controls with ’partially effective’ ratings are prioritized for remediation and funding reviews in Q3 2026.

31. Committee oversight enforces owner accountabilities, escalation thresholds, and consolidated executive reporting. Owners must submit mitigation plans, KPI progress, and a residual risk forecast seven days before each meeting. Noncompliant items escalate to the CRO for remediation timelines and funding decisions. Status updates are published internally weekly.
